annotations.text:
THE TILE

One shape whether or not artwork exists, which is what makes the two modes interchangeable in a row.

HEAD, 16:10. Either an uploaded image, or a generated composition: a tone-on-tone diamond lattice over a corner glow, the amount set in Oswald with a single gold gradient clipped to the text, and a bevel and glow from two drop shadows. One kicker, one figure, one line. Content sits bottom-left so the top air can carry the seal.

FOOT. The player's own progress, or the one action worth a button. Always system-drawn, so uploading artwork never costs you personalisation.

One metal for the whole family, like a tournament set. Variety comes from the artwork, not from four different accent colours.

Layout is unchanged — hero, then offers under it. Only the card changed.

The expiry bar moved above the strip and out of the card set. It is player state, not an offer, so it is never artwork and never sits in the row.

The VIP-scoped weekly rule stays off every player surface: a targeted rule must not be advertised to someone who cannot receive it.

The artwork on these tiles is a drawn placeholder standing in for an uploaded asset, not a real banner. Figures are sample values and the copy is English only.

ARTWORK UPLOAD

One 16:10 image per promotion, 1280 x 800 or larger. No separate mobile crop — the same asset works at both sizes because the tile keeps its ratio.

A wrong aspect is refused rather than cropped. Silently cropping cuts the headline off somebody's finished design, which is exactly what the existing hero banner code already avoids.

The preview renders the real tile at real size, beside the generated fallback, so the admin can see what removing the image would do before they do it.

This needs an artwork field per promotion plus the existing upload storage. The welcome bonus is a site setting today, so it needs somewhere to hang its own image.

The list's old hero flag is now a real artwork column: a thumbnail when one is uploaded, a Generated tag when not.

Cashback pays at period close on these screens, not at the first hourly run that sees the threshold crossed. The numbers assume it.

The three lower screens show the content area only. The sidebar is the one drawn on the list screen above.

Balance adjustment on the player Bonuses tab sits in the admin scope. It is reachable by clerks today, with no cap and no record of who did it.
